title: Director, Supplier Quality
text:
We’re here for one reason and one reason only – to cure cancer. Every moment is dedicated to developing treatments and every action moves us one step closer to our goal. We’ve made incredible scientific breakthroughs and our pioneering personalized CAR T-cell therapies have changed the paradigm. But we're not finished yet.

 

Join Kite, as we make even bigger advances in cancer therapies, and help shape where our business and medical science goes next.

 

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfill their aspirations. Join Kite and help create more tomorrows.

**Job Description**
-------------------

We are seeking a highly motivated individual to join our team as Director, Supplier Quality to be the Compliance and Technical Lead for the global quality network of Supplier Quality Management. This role will report to the Sr. Director, External and Supplier Quality. Key responsibilities include overseeing all Quality aspects associated with global suppliers and vendors while acting as a point of contact for compliance and technical issues.

**Responsibilities:**

* Serves as the Quality lead for Company’s global suppliers and vendors.
* Develop and lead the global Supplier Quality Management (SQM) strategy, governance model, procedures, and operating standards.
* Define supplier segmentation and oversight requirements based on GMP criticality, material/service risk, patient impact, and supply-chain risk.
* Establish supplier quality KPIs and scorecards covering areas
* Provide leadership for significant supplier-related deviations, nonconformances, investigations, and Supplier Corrective Action Requests (SCARs).
* Ensure adequate root-cause analysis and scientifically justified CAPAs.
* Monitor CAPA effectiveness and recurring supplier issues.
* Lead risk assessments for changes in supplier status, manufacturing location, process, specifications, ownership, regulatory status, or business continuity.
* Evaluate quality risks associated with single-source materials, long lead-time materials, critical raw materials, and constrained suppliers.
* Partner with Supply Chain and Technical Operations to balance GMP compliance, patient safety, product quality, and supply continuity when supplier risks emerge
* Ensure audit observations are appropriately classified, investigated, responded to, and closed.
* Maintain the supplier quality system in a continuous state of inspection readiness.
* Lead escalation for chronic supplier performance problems and determine when additional controls, suspension, or disqualification are appropriate.
* May write or support review of quality agreements to ensure scope of work, compliance and testing requirements are defined accurately, including metrics, quality deliverables.
* Supports data gathering, analysis and compilation for Annual Product Reviews (APR) and Annual Vector Reviews (AVR) where applicable.
Up to 25% travel (both domestic and international) 

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Advanced scientific degree (i.e. MD, PharmD, PhD) and 8+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing, OR
* Master’s Degree and 10+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing, OR
* Bachelor’s Degree and 12+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing, OR
High School Degree and 16+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing 

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced science degree.
* Deep knowledge and experience in quality assurance in a highly regulated manufacturing environment.
* Well versed in Compliance, Auditing, Validation, and testing of biopharmaceuticals, preferred.
* Working knowledge of Quality Systems
* Working knowledge of current regulatory requirements (FDA/EMA, JP)
* Minimum 6 years of Compliance/QA and/or QC lab management experience in the biotech and/or pharmaceutical industry
* Strong knowledge of current GMP, SOPs and quality control processes
* Identifying, writing evaluating and closing OOS’s and investigations
* Strong knowledge or ability to understand/interpret manufacturing processes
* Process/Equipment/laboratory instrument IQ/OQ/PQ/PV
* Prior people management experience.
* Proficient in MS Word, Excel, Power Point and other applications
* Ability to communicate effectively (written, verbal) and work independently with scientific/technical personnel.
* Comfortable in a fast-paced company environment with minimal direction and able to adjust workload based upon changing priorities
* Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and willing to accept temporary responsibilities outside of initial job description
* Ability to think critically and demonstrate troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
* Ability to exercise judgement and take appropriate action where precedent may not exist
Excellent interpersonal, verbal, written and presentation communication skills 

 

**People Leader Accountabilities:**

* Create Inclusion - knowing the business value of diverse teams, modeling inclusion, and embedding the value of diversity in the way they manage their teams.
* Develop Talent - understand the skills, experience, aspirations and potential of their employees and coach them on current performance and future potential. They ensure employees are receiving the feedback and insight needed to grow, develop and realize their purpose.
Empower Teams - connect the team to the organization by aligning goals, purpose, and organizational objectives, and holding them to account. They provide the support needed to remove barriers and connect their team to the broader ecosystem. 

 
The salary range for this position is: $191,250.00 - $247,500.00. Kite considers a variety of factors when determining base compensation, including experience, qualifications, and geographic location. These considerations mean actual compensation will vary. This position may also be eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, discretionary stock-based long-term incentives (eligibility may vary based on role), paid time off, and a benefits package. Benefits include company-sponsored medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans\*.

For additional benefits information, visit:

https://www.gilead.com/careers/compensation-benefits-and-wellbeing

\* Eligible employees may participate in benefit plans, subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans.

Kite is a biopharmaceutical company engaged in the development of innovative cancer immunotherapies with a goal of providing rapid, long-term durable response and eliminating the burden of chronic care. The company is focused on chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) and T cell receptor (TCR) engineered cell therapies designed to empower the immune system's ability to recognize and kill tumors. Kite is based in Santa Monica, CA. For more information on Kite, please visit www.kitepharma.com . Sign up to follow @KitePharma on Twitter at www.twitter.com/kitepharma .
